title: input_parity_reject's selection assert can never fire (unsatisfiable && over mutually-exclusive fields)
detail: The W7-fold scenario (added in d91109e) promises 'a rejected draw must not change the selection', but sel_node/sel_pipe are mutually exclusive by construction, so both != -1 simultaneously is impossible. The condition is dead; a regression that sets exactly one passes.
recommended_fix: Change the gate to `r.sel_node != -1 || r.sel_pipe != -1` so a selection change on either field fails the pin.

title: input_parity_pad_cursor asserts only the final cursor; the promised first-Up-lands-on-last-node boundary is unpinned
detail: Only the post-run state (pad_node == 0) is checked. If Dpad_Up were dropped by controller_map, Dpad_Down's first placement lands on node 0 (idx = 0 for step >= 0) — identical final state, so the pin passes with the Up boundary broken.
recommended_fix: Split into two scenarios (Up-only asserts pad_node == 2; Up-then-Down asserts the wrap to 0) or capture the mid-script cursor.

title: run_input_parity cleanup frees the frame slices but never the sc.mouse/touch/pad dynamic arrays themselves
detail: frames() heap-allocates each scenario's [dynamic][]Device_Event backing; the defer deletes the element slices + expected but not the three per-device array headers. Small exit-time leak in a file that otherwise documents ownership meticulously; the harness runs no tracking allocator, so CI never catches it.
recommended_fix: Add delete(sc.mouse); delete(sc.touch); delete(sc.pad) alongside the existing per-frame deletes in the cleanup defer.
